title: The Editor Interface
description: Walk through every major window: Scene, Game, Hierarchy, Inspector, Project, and Console.

slides.title: The Default Layout 🖼️
slides.content:
# Windows of the Unity Editor

When you open a project, you'll see several panels. The default layout includes:

*   **Scene View** – your interactive 3D/2D canvas.
*   **Game View** – what the player will see (rendered by your camera).
*   **Hierarchy** – list of all GameObjects in the current scene.
*   **Inspector** – properties of the currently selected object.
*   **Project** – your Assets folder, displayed as thumbnails or list.
*   **Console** – debug messages, errors, and warnings.

quizData.question: Which window shows the list of all objects in your current scene?
quizData.explanation: The Hierarchy shows every GameObject currently placed in the open scene.

slides.title: Customizing Your Workspace 🛠️
slides.content:
# Layouts and Docking

*   You can drag any tab to dock it elsewhere or turn it into a floating window.
*   Use the **Layout** dropdown (top‑right) to switch between presets like "2 by 3", "Tall", or "Default".
*   Save your own layout by selecting **Layout → Save Layout...** for quick switching.

quizData.question: You can only use the default layout provided by Unity.
quizData.explanation: Unity allows you to completely customize and save window layouts.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Quick Reset

If you ever mess up your layout, go to **Window → Layouts → Default** to restore the original arrangement.
